sa15:1.2: One time, the Buddha was staying at Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park in Jeta’s Grove of Śrāvastī.
sa15:2.1: At the time, a certain monk came to the Buddha.
sa15:2.2: He bowed his head at the Buddha’s feet, withdrew to stand to one side, and then said,
sa15:2.3: “It’d be good, Bhagavān, if you would briefly explain the Dharma for me now.
sa15:2.4: After hearing the Dharma, I’ll go alone to a quiet place and cultivate it earnestly.
sa15:2.5: After cultivating it earnestly, I’ll again contemplate:
sa15:2.6: ‘A good son leaves home, cuts off his hair and beard, puts on the Dharma robes, is a believer in the homeless, and leaves home [to train on the path].
sa15:2.7: That’s the way he reaches the ultimate and unsurpassed religious practice.
sa15:2.8: He’ll realize in the present life:
sa15:2.9: “My births have been ended, the religious practice has been established, and the task has been accomplished.”
sa15:2.10: He himself will know he won’t be subject to a later existence.’”
sa15:3.2: “Good, good! Monk, I’m glad you’ve said,
sa15:3.3: ‘[Bhagavān,] give me a brief explanation of the Dharma.
sa15:3.4: From that brief explanation of the Dharma, I will get a full understanding of its meaning.
sa15:3.5: I’ll go alone to a quiet place, focus on contemplation, and live earnestly … up to …
sa15:3.6: “‘I myself know that I won’t be subject to a later existence.’”’
sa15:4.1: The monk said to the Buddha,
sa15:5.2: “Listen closely! Listen closely, and consider it well.
sa15:5.3: I will explain this for you.
sa15:5.4: Monk, if something brings about the tendencies, then it brings about death.
sa15:5.5: If something brings about death, then it’s bound by grasping.
sa15:5.6: Monk, if it doesn’t bring about the tendencies, then it won’t bring about death.
sa15:5.7: If something doesn’t bring about death, then it’s freed from grasping.”
sa15:6.1: The monk said to the Buddha,
sa15:7.2: “How do you understand the meaning of my brief explanation of the Dharma in full?”
sa15:8.1: The monk said to the Buddha,
sa15:8.2: “Bhagavān, form brings about the tendencies, and form brings about death.
sa15:8.3: Something that brings about the tendencies and death is bound by grasping.
sa15:8.4: Thus, feeling … conception … volition … awareness brings about the tendencies, and awareness brings about death.
sa15:8.5: Something that brings about the tendencies and brings about death is bound by grasping.
sa15:9.1: “Bhagavān, if form doesn’t bring about the tendencies, it won’t bring about death.
sa15:9.2: Something that doesn’t bring about the tendencies and doesn’t bring about death is freed from grasping.
sa15:9.3: Thus, if feeling … conception … volition … awareness doesn’t bring about the tendencies, it won’t bring about death.
sa15:9.4: Something that doesn’t bring about the tendencies and doesn’t bring about death is freed from grasping.
sa15:9.5: I understand the Bhagavān’s brief explanation of the Dharma in this way.”
sa15:10.2: “Good! It’s good, monk, that you understand the meaning of my brief explanation of the Dharma in full.
sa15:10.4: If form brings about the tendencies, it brings about death.
sa15:10.5: Something that brings about the tendencies and brings about death is bound by grasping.
sa15:10.6: Thus, if feeling … conception … volition … awareness brings about the tendencies, it brings about death.
sa15:10.7: Something that brings about the tendencies and brings about death is bound by grasping.
sa15:11.1: “Monk, if form doesn’t bring about the tendencies, it won’t bring about death.
sa15:11.2: Something that doesn’t bring about the tendencies and doesn’t bring about death is freed from grasping.
sa15:11.3: Thus, if feeling … conception … volition … awareness doesn’t bring about the tendencies, it won’t bring about death.
sa15:11.4: Something that doesn’t bring about the tendencies and doesn’t bring about death is freed from grasping.”
sa15:12.1: When that monk heard what the Buddha taught, he felt great joy.
sa15:12.2: He bowed to the Buddha and withdrew.
sa15:12.3: He went alone to a quiet place where he diligently trained and lived earnestly.
sa15:12.4: After diligently training and living earnestly, he thought,
sa15:12.5: “A good son leaves home, cuts off his hair and beard, puts on the Dharma robes, is a believer in the homeless, and leaves home … up to …
sa15:12.6: ‘I myself know that I won’t be subject to a later existence.’”
sa15:13.1: That monk then became an arhat, and his mind was liberated.
